findings.title: Claude edits more than it reads
findings.explanation: Claude made 2210 reads and 1519 edits (ratio 1.5:1). A healthy ratio is 4+ reads per edit. Editing without reading leads to retries and wasted tokens.

fix.label: Add to your CLAUDE.md:
fix.text: Before editing any file, read it first. Before modifying a function, grep for all callers. Research before you edit.

findings.title: 1 MCP server should be project-scoped
findings.explanation: These MCP servers look useful in a small set of projects but are loaded into other projects where they are not invoked. Project-scoping them keeps the hot-project workflow while avoiding their tool lines elsewhere. claude_ai_Claude_Docs: 90% of 10 calls in E:\GitHub\Atlas (8 calls), E:\Projects\fashion-app (1 call); loaded but unused in C:\Users\jakeh (24 loaded sessions), E:\GitHub\wholesomenfl.com (6 loaded sessions), E:\GitHub\Atlas\.claude\worktrees\agent-a04e9f05b8b583c3c (2 loaded sessions), +115 more.

findings.title: Shrink bash output limit
findings.explanation: Your bash output cap is 30K chars (default). Most output fits in 15K. The extra ~3.8K tokens per bash call is trailing noise.

findings.explanation: In ~/.claude/skills/ but not invoked this period: phase-dispatch, unslop. Each adds ~80 tokens of metadata to every session.

findings.explanation: Edit turns using these capabilities are retry-heavy: MCP server claude-in-chrome: 6/11 edit turns retried (55%), 6 retries across 4 projects. This is a correlation report, not proof of causation; compare the retry-heavy turns with one-shot turns before changing MCP scope or skill instructions.

Do not remove a capability solely because it appears in this report.

findings.title: Claude is re-reading the same files
findings.explanation: 44 redundant re-reads across sessions. Top repeats: n.html (9x), app.js (5x), session.rs (3x). Each re-read loads the same content into context again.

fix.label: Point Claude at exact locations in your prompt, for example:
fix.text: In <file> lines <start>-<end>, look at the <function> function.

findings.title: 2 sessions with a low cache hit rate
findings.explanation: These sessions read less than 80% of their input from the prompt cache: E--Projects-fashion-app/4f88f0bd-ce65-459b-bf39-3dde68f4e989 (Claude): 75.2% of 108.9K input; E--Projects-fashion-app/e81f01ba-b7f6-4821-b243-86ff980a8548 (Claude): 76.0% of 99.4K input. Healthy agent sessions usually sit above 80%. Low rates come from switching models or tools mid-session, editing instruction files mid-session, or long pauses that let the cache expire, so the full prompt is paid again.

fix.label: Keep the prompt cache valid:
fix.text: Stay on one model per session, and start a new session after editing instruction files or MCP config instead of continuing the old one.

findings.title: 12 context-heavy sessions
findings.explanation: Effective input/cache tokens swamp output in these sessions: E--GitHub-Atlas/ffe704e0-5958-453b-9860-484a01d6e47d on 2026-11-01: 12.8M effective input/cache vs 191.2K output (67.2:1, 7.2x previous session input); E--Projects-fashion-app/0ed4a733-c810-4470-a0bd-d128efaae0be on 2026-10-17: 6.7M effective input/cache vs 199.6K output (33.5:1); C--Users-jakeh-source-wholesomenfl-com/5dd443a2-dda3-45cf-ba6b-f85d01c418f7 on 2026-10-05: 3.3M effective input/cache vs 76.5K output (43.6:1); E--GitHub-Atlas/0400e6e0-f304-4c1e-9dc4-6b4f145ddde1 on 2026-10-22: 2.2M effective input/cache vs 45.5K output (47.5:1); C--Users-jakeh/2ca088b1-5ec3-4fe4-a1db-c3658b541280 on 2026-11-04: 2.5M effective input/cache vs 82.1K output (30.0:1, 67.6x previous session input); +7 more. This can come from stale context carryover, inherently context-heavy work, or abandoned runs that loaded too much context; starting fresh with only the current goal and relevant files can cut repeated prompt overhead.
